question: Will Hormuz commercial shipping resume to >=50 daily transits (7-day avg) before EOD 2026-06-10?
delta_reason: RESOLVED-NO (early, 7 days before horizon). Commercial transit collapsed to ~4 vessels/day (4% of pre-crisis ~95/day baseline per IMF PortWatch last published 2026-05-24). Maersk/MSC/CMA CGM/Hapag-Lloyd remain suspended; Lloyd's war-risk insurance at 8.0x pre-crisis; 6 P&I clubs withdrew cover; Iran suspended talks 1 Jun and reiterated full-closure posture. Reaching >=50 transits/day averaged over 7 consecutive days by 10 Jun requires a 12x increase in 7 days — physically impossible without an immediate signed deal (probability ~0.05 per F2) plus instantaneous mine clearance. Early resolution avoids carrying a forecast whose outcome is certain.
resolution_criteria: YES if Hormuz Strait Monitor (or UNCTAD, or Lloyd's List) reports >=50 daily transits averaged over 7 consecutive days within the horizon window. NO if average stays below 50/day for the full horizon window.
resolution_source_rule: Hormuz Strait Monitor / IMF PortWatch (primary), Lloyd's List Intelligence (secondary), UNCTAD Maritime Trade quarterly (lagging).
ambiguity_rule: Dark-fleet/Iranian-flagged-only count with Western insurers still refusing = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. PGSA addendum: third-country vessels under Iran's PGSA toll regime count ONLY IF >=2 of Hormuz Strait Monitor/Lloyd's List/UNCTAD/Windward confirm them independent; PGSA self-reported excluded.
